name: Bloodhoof Village
summary: At Bloodhoof Village beside Stonebull Lake, young tauren prepare for the road to Thunder Bluff. Baine Bloodhoof leads them, while the village tends Mulgore’s defense, trade, and rites.

sections.title: Heart of the Plains
sections.body: Beside Stonebull Lake in central Mulgore, Bloodhoof Village is where young tauren come after their trials at Camp Narache. They hone their skills here before traveling to the great mesas of Thunder Bluff. Patient breeders tame wild kodo beasts for travel, and the village is also a center of craft and ceremony.

sections.title: Leadership and Rites
sections.body:
Baine Bloodhoof, son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, oversees daily rule and the region’s defense. Braves patrol the grasslands against aggressive wildlife, quilboar encroachers, and the Venture Company.

Spiritual guides such as Zarlman Two-Moons tend to the tribe’s inner life. They lead novices through sacred journeys, including the Rite of Vision.

aliases: who is in charge of bloodhoof village
faq.answer: Baine Bloodhoof, son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, leads Bloodhoof Village and directs its defenses against threats to the central plains.

faq.q: What major rites are conducted here?
faq.answer: Spiritual guides such as Zarlman Two-Moons lead young tauren through the traditional Rite of Vision, an essential spiritual journey on the path to adulthood.

faq.q: What is the settlement known for producing?
faq.answer: At Bloodhoof Village, patient breeders tame and train wild plains kodos as mounts.

faq.q: Where do travelers go after finishing their tasks here?
faq.answer: After their deeds in central Mulgore, travelers are generally directed north to Thunder Bluff, the tauren capital.

angles.text: For young tauren, entering Bloodhoof Village marks their first real step beyond youth and into wider tribal responsibility and spiritual maturity.
For the Horde, Bloodhoof Village offers a peaceful stopover and a vital link between Mulgore’s southern plains and the Horde capital at Thunder Bluff.
